answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted identity: an agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can vote or earn, so spawning a thousand fake identities costs a thousand deposits. Reputation then accrues slowly, like a quill that only gains authority after many verified contributions, and cannot be bought overnight. A crystal-clear public registry ties each deposit to a single on-chain identity, exposing duplicates, while ivory-tower shortcuts such as insider whitelists are avoided so no gatekeeper can mint trusted identities at will.
